slides.title: You made it, it is yours
slides.text: A drawing you make is yours, because you made it. Finding something online does not make it yours. The maker decides how their work may be used.
slides.alt: Would you rather share a drawing so everyone can see it, or show it only to your family?

focus.cue: Your drawing, shown to everyone online
Your drawing, kept to family only

slides.title: Read the badge
slides.text: Every piece of work carries a simple badge. Some badges say ask first, and some say give credit. Public domain work is free for anyone.
steps: credit badge: use it and give credit
slides.alt: Would you rather use a picture someone else made and credit them, or draw your own from scratch?

focus.cue: Use a picture someone else made, and credit them
Or draw your own, even if it is worse

slides.title: Photos need a yes
slides.text: Sharing a photo of someone else needs their yes, always. If a friend posts a photo of you that you do not like, ask them to take it down. If it stays up, tell a trusted adult, who can help report it.
slides.alt: Would you rather share one photo with the whole world, or ten photos with just ten friends?

focus.cue: One photo, shared with the whole world
Ten photos, shared with ten friends

slides.title: My keep-private rule
slides.text: Some things stay private, always: your address, your school and your passphrase. Say your own rule out loud. These are mine to keep.
slides.alt: The mailbox key builder: pick words for a passphrase, the key that locks your mailbox in Packet Post.

focus.cue: In the game, your passphrase is your mailbox key
Words nobody could guess about you

slides.title: The Magpie's nest
slides.text: The Magpie pins photos of other birds in its nest without asking. Now the other birds have stopped visiting. Asking first is how sharers keep their friends.
slides.alt: Would you rather share one photo with the whole world, or ten photos with just ten friends?

focus.cue: One photo, shared with the whole world
Ten photos, shared with ten friends

words.means: a yes from the maker to use their work
picking one thing instead of another

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Would You Rather, choose the Online topic, and play Online: share or keep. Then write the credit line for a game you might make. Last, name one thing you keep private.
slides.alt: A Would You Rather online dilemma: something you made, and the choice of whether to share it or keep it.

focus.cue: Play Online: share or keep, and judge each pair
